## This week

Reasoning, the intermediate steps before the answer, and two ways to get it: prompting (chain of thought, ReAct) and its limits, and reasoning models that are trained to write their own steps, with when to use one. How such a model is built: the training stages of an LLM, supervised finetuning and reinforcement learning, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, pure reinforcement learning (DeepSeek-R1-Zero), SFT combined with RL (DeepSeek-R1), and distillation into smaller models; the four ways to build and improve reasoning models compared. A reasoning model in an agent: the planner with faster models carrying out the steps, and reasoning effort.

## Practice and lab

The practice builds MCP servers over TheMealDB, a public web API of recipes, with the MCP Python SDK, and gives their tools to an agent made with `create_agent`. The same two questions (two meals with chicken breast and garlic; Italian seafood) run on two servers: one with a tool for each of the eleven requests of the API, and one with a tool for each task of the user (`find_meals`, `get_recipe`), built by two principles of Anthropic's guide for writers of tools: one call for one task of the user, and a small result. In Part 5 each student chooses one of four public APIs (Open-Meteo, Open Library, Frankfurter, OpenAlex), writes the tasks of its users and one tool for each task, without code, and presents the design in class. The APIs need no key.
